title: US consumer confidence falls to its weakest reading since 2014
summary: The Conference Board's consumer confidence index fell 6.7 points to 81.9 in September, far below the 89.2 economists expected and the weakest reading in more than twelve years. The present-situation measure dropped 7.9 points to 109.3 and the expectations index fell to 63.6, its third straight monthly decline, while twelve-month inflation expectations rose to 6.1%. Separately, Labor Department data showed job openings falling 256,000 in August to 7.079 million, leaving 1.01 vacancies per unemployed person.
